title: Unity AI Assistant
author: CoBuddyDev
selftext:
There are alot of tools out there. Claude, Codex, Copilot, and about a million websites.

Alot of them are genuinely good tools.

  
However they are all also general purpose tools.

  
I am working on a Unity AI assistant that is completely context aware of your project, takes your overall vision into consideration with every action. It can write scripts for you, do things in Unity (basically anything you can do yourself it can execute for you minus a couple of things) and build huge projects. 

Now the distinction is this is not a single prompt->game workflow. Obviously making an actual functional and scalable game in Unity takes alot more than that. However this tool accelerates workflows like never before and drastically improves both speed and accuracy of your development. There are also built in optimization tools and code health tools to make sure the AI isn't wiring up some spaghetti for you.

All that being said: I am looking for a business partner. The software is done. It just needs someone who is willing to run the business side. If this sounds like something you would be interested please reach out to me in DMs and I would love to discuss it further!

  
THIS IS NOT AN AD. The software is unreleased. This is just to reach out and see if anyone shares an interest in the product!

comments.author: Seven-Prime
comments.body: How would this compare to CoplayDev or Unity's AI assistant?

replies.author: CoBuddyDev
replies.body:
Coplay feels more like a fast-moving experimenter’s tool. It can be useful if you want something aggressive and are comfortable with a looser workflow, but the interface feels pretty narrow and, from my impression, it leans more toward “let the assistant take a swing” than giving you a really disciplined production loop.

Unity’s AI assistant has the advantage of being native to the editor and officially integrated, which is appealing. The tradeoff is that it’s still Unity’s general-purpose answer to AI in the editor, so it feels more like broad platform functionality than something deeply obsessed with the day-to-day reality of shipping inside one project. It’s convenient, but not necessarily where I’d expect the strongest project-specific execution and trust layer yet.

CoBuddy is aiming at a different standard. The goal isn’t just to have AI in Unity or to generate quick actions. It’s to be genuinely grounded in the connected project, make changes with more structure, and give the user a clearer sense of what happened, what changed, and how to recover if something goes wrong. So compared to Coplay, it’s less “loose cannon copilot” and more deliberate, production-minded assistant. Compared to Unity’s assistant, it’s less about being the default built-in AI surface and more about going deeper on reliability, project awareness, and execution quality for real Unity work. It also takes your GDD into account alot better and will maintain that as its vision as it works with you in Unity.
